input: Plan a gap year itinerary before graduate school

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: A gap year can mean pure travel, skill-building, volunteering, working, or a mix — this fundamentally changes what goes into the itinerary.
Budget is the single biggest limiter: it determines how many destinations, what accommodation level, and whether paid work needs to be built in.
The exact start and end dates of the gap year (departure date and grad school start) define the total time available and how tightly it must be scheduled.
Traveling solo vs. with a partner or group changes logistics, pacing, destination choice, and safety planning entirely.
Whether they have a home base or visa/passport constraints narrows or widens which regions are even feasible to include.
The balance between adventure, cultural immersion, rest, and professional development shapes what kinds of experiences to prioritise in the plan.
Knowing what 'a great gap year' means to this person — personal growth, specific skills, seeing certain places — determines how to evaluate and sequence choices.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a gap year itinerary before graduate school
gold.taskDescription: Design a structured gap year plan covering destinations, activities, and timelines for the period between now and the start of graduate school.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the entire gap year?
questions.description: Understanding the overall financial envelope determines destination feasibility, accommodation style, and whether paid work or stipends need to be factored into the itinerary.

questions.title: What are your exact gap year start and end dates?
questions.description: Pinning down the precise window between now and the first day of grad school defines total time available and how densely the itinerary can be packed.

questions.title: What is the primary purpose of your gap year?
questions.description: Clarifying whether the year is mainly for travel, volunteering, language learning, professional experience, rest, or a combination determines the entire structure of the plan.

questions.title: Will you be traveling solo or with others?
questions.description: Knowing whether companions are involved changes pacing, destination selection, booking logistics, and how much flexibility to build into the itinerary.

questions.title: Which regions or countries are you targeting, if any?
questions.description: Identifying geographic priorities or visa constraints narrows the feasible destination pool and informs routing and travel-time between stops.

questions.title: How do you want to balance adventure, culture, and downtime?
questions.description: Understanding the preferred rhythm and experience type — high-energy exploration vs. slow immersion vs. restorative rest — shapes how each segment of the itinerary is designed.

questions.title: What would make this gap year feel truly successful to you?
questions.description: Defining the personal benchmark for success — whether that is specific skills gained, places seen, or a feeling of readiness for grad school — sets the north star for every planning decision.
